blind.why: Match-pacing charts (round length, first tag, tags/round, plant/attacker-win/quick-round rates; 14 Pro-vs-Pro rounds, seeds 4+11, vs CS2 MR12 norms). The other side has a hard floor: no round ends under 45 s, round length p10 is 60 s with a spike at 60-75 s, and attackers win 71% (10/14) and plant 71%. The ref has quick rounds, post-plant tails and a 48% attacker win rate.

Crosshair error vs time since the enemy is first visible (82 Pro engagements at 50 Hz). The ref waits about 200 ms of reaction, then flicks and settles. Ours starts closing the error at once: median 12.7° at t=0, 6.7° at 0.1 s, 2.8° at 0.2 s. Some first shots land within 0.1 s, which reads as aim assist.

6-frame POV fight strips (shots/critic-bots/strip_b0.png vs CS2 trailer_1 at 35.6-37.4 s). In the CS2 duels several shots are traded and the fight is readable. Ours: the crosshair is on a few-pixel enemy at 24 m one frame after it appears, and a single Pip tap crowns it. The fight is over in about 0.36 s with no exchange.

biggest_gap: Bots aim before they have reacted. In brain.js the aim intent (around line 428) picks the most recently SEEN memory entry by seenT. Perception updates seenT on the first visible tick, long before the reaction window marks the enemy `spotted`, and the intent tracks its exact position plus velocity lead with fast=true. Measured (shots/critic-bots/aim2.mjs 21 pro): median crosshair error drops 14.3° to 2.3° between first sight and acquisition, so the bot is already on target when its 'reaction' ends. Even 0.12 s blinks that are never noticed snap the view 15-25° toward the enemy (45°→22°, 43°→22°) and keep it there for 1.6 s. Rookies do the same (14.3°→10.0° in 0.1 s). This makes peeking pointless and leaks information. CS2/humans: no crosshair motion for about 180-250 ms, then a flick with over/undershoot and a corrective sub-movement. Fix: only spotted (or heard/called) memory may drive the aim intent, and the flick starts after react.
other_gaps: Pacing and side balance. Over 14 Pro-v-Pro rounds Ember won 10 and planted in 71%. No round ended under 45 s (p10 60 s). The position heatmap (shots/critic-bots/heat.png) shows Tide never leaves its half: no early aggression, no info pushes, no CT-side picks. Ember has no fast eco rush or fake. CS2 runs about 48% T wins, about 20% of rounds under 45 s, and CTs that sometimes take map control.

Fights are too short and too accurate to read. The shot hit rate is 48-59% (telemetry hits/shots; CS2 humans are about 18-25%). The median engagement lasts 0.48 s at 21 m, it takes about 8 shots per tag-out, and a single pistol tap often crowns at over 20 m. There are almost no traded sprays or re-peeks.

Difficulty is too steep at the bottom. Elite (Ember) vs Rookie (Tide) went 6-0 by elimination with 30 tags to 0, and Rookies acquired a target and fired only 5 times in 6 rounds. Rookies need to be beatable, not inert.

Movement is always loud. 92% of moving samples run at 6-7 m/s and bots almost never shift-walk, so lurkers, site approaches and retakes give away footsteps. 28% of Pro shots are fired faster than 1.5 m/s, despite the counter-strafe gate.

Callouts are thin spam: 155 'enemy' plus area lines in 6 rounds (26 per round), often 3 bots calling the same contact within a second (e.g. Kilo/Vesper/You 'enemy A Site'). They carry no count, weapon, 'last seen' or 'one low', and there is no dedupe per team.

Clumping and plant logic. All 5 Ember funnel through Long in single file, and the carrier's POV sits inside a teammate's back for about 0.5 s (strip_a1.png). About 4% of shots pass within 0.45 m of a teammate before reaching the target (Rook→Kilo, Tempo→Rook). At A site during a live firefight the carrier stares into a crate face 1 m away with 'HOLD TO ARM', neither planting nor fighting (strip_a2.png).
bugs: Aim intent uses unspotted sightings (spec violation: 'blinks shorter than the window are never noticed' is false for aim)

The bundled bot_test gate failed on seed 4: 'cpu 1.60 ms/frame > 1.5' (0.80 ms/tick, max tick 672 ms). This was measured with machine load at 70-110, so it may be contaminated, but the gate does not hold under contention. Elite-v-Rookie run: 0.52 ms/tick.
Dead bots keep a live-looking state in the bot-lab panel (e.g. Echo hp 0 'hold/shoot tgt=Halo9').
strengths: Robust: 0 exceptions and 0 console errors in all runs, 100% of rounds free of stuck bots, 0-2 teleports per run
No real wallhack: kills never come without LOS, aim within 4° of a hidden, unknown enemy 0.6% of the time (below chance), and only 5% of shots are fired with no LOS (known-angle sprays)

Plausible structure: executes, rotations, retakes and disarms all happen with matching callouts, kill-distance spread is sensible (median about 18 m), sight-to-first-shot is about 350-410 ms for Pro and 275 ms for Elite, and median speed at the shot is 0 (counter-strafe mostly works)
Utility is used every round (12-22 throws per 6-8 rounds) and difficulty separates clearly (Elite sight-to-shot 275 ms vs Rookie 510 ms)
